items.title: XRP hovers at $1 with record leverage ahead of CPI
points: XRP briefly touched 99 cents Tuesday — its lowest since November 2024 — before bouncing to $1.02, where the recovery stalled.
Open interest in XRP futures (total value of outstanding leveraged bets) hit 2.67 billion XRP ($2.73 billion), the highest since October.
July CPI (Consumer Price Index, the main US inflation gauge) is forecast at 0.1% monthly growth and 3.4% year-on-year; a hot print could push XRP below $1 toward 92-cent support.
Options markets price only a 1.3% post-CPI move for bitcoin, the kind of complacency that often precedes surprises.

items.title: Hacker drains $200,000 from XRP bridge via fake deposits
points: Attacker manipulated the bridge's relayer code (software that verifies and relays transfers between blockchains) to log deposits that never delivered XRP to the reserve wallet.
The bridge issued valid receipt tokens for the empty deposits, and 17 of 28 relayers approved payouts because their records showed legitimate deposits.
The exploit ran 97 minutes on August 9, caused by relayer code processing bridge memos without verifying the destination address.
Operator tx halted the bridge, patched the flaw and hired forensics specialists; ChangeNOW froze part of the stolen funds as they moved through multiple addresses.

items.title: Fidelity files to add staking and quarterly dividends to $898M ether ETF
points: Fidelity's Ethereum Fund (FETH) could stake up to 100% of its ether (locking tokens to help validate transactions in exchange for rewards), keeping some liquid for redemptions.
The fund would keep 85% of gross staking rewards after paying node operators Blockdaemon, Figment and Galaxy, with net rewards covering expenses then paid out quarterly in cash.

An IRS safe harbor from November 2025 permits crypto trusts to stake without losing the grantor-trust tax status ETFs rely on; Grayscale and 21Shares already added staking and BlackRock launched a separate product.
The change turns ether ETFs into dividend-paying products, a structural edge over bitcoin (which cannot be staked) while ether underperforms.

items.title: SEC to propose a token safe harbor
points: The SEC plans a framework setting objective conditions tokens must meet to avoid being classified as securities (investments subject to strict registration rules).
Qualifying tokens could operate without registration while still meeting investor-protection standards.
It marks a shift from defining crypto's boundaries through enforcement actions toward proactive rule-making.
Backers argue clear rules could reverse the exodus of projects that delayed launches or moved offshore, and may become a template for regulators abroad.

items.title: Vitalik Buterin's Ethereum 2026 'Strawmap' adds seven priorities
points: Quantum safety becomes a first-class priority, backed by leanSPHINCS signatures and post-quantum aggregation against future quantum-computer attacks.
Native rollups arrive via maturing SNARKs (cryptographic proofs that verify a computation without revealing its data), plus blob and gas futures for dynamic pricing of blockchain resources.
zkzk frames would expose non-EVM instruction sets (leanISA, RISC-V) at protocol level, demoting the EVM (Ethereum's standard computation engine) from enshrined feature to intermediate representation.
Privacy gets protocol-level treatment (keyed nonces, FOCIL, lean privacy pools, wormholes) and recursive STARKs span execution, consensus and data layers.
State expiry is dropped for specialized state types tuned to token transfers, swaps and privacy; VDFs (verifiable delay functions) and many EVM tweaks are deprioritized.

items.title: EIP-8363 staking taper could destabilize onchain credit markets
points: The proposal tapers consensus rewards to zero net issuance (no new ETH minted for validation) at 60.25M ETH staked, about 50% of supply, cutting validator income roughly 50%.
MEV (maximal extractable value — profits validators earn by ordering or including transactions strategically) is untouched, so it would become a larger share of validator revenue.

LST looping (borrowing stablecoins against liquid staking tokens to re-stake and amplify yield) drives most ETH lending yield, yet the proposal models no downstream effect on borrowers repaying WETH debt or deposit APYs.
LSTs are ~40% of onchain TVL (total value locked), $2.6B of stablecoin debt is backed by ETH/LSTs, and $11.4B of ETF and treasury inflows hold 7.8M ETH.
Post-Merge net ETH issuance is already 0.30%/year versus Bitcoin 0.82%, gold 1.7% and M2 money supply 5.5%; authors urge modeling MEV burn first.

items.title: Mastercard closes $1.8B BVNK deal as on-chain growth plateaus
points: BVNK brings $23B in trailing twelve-month settlement volume to Mastercard.
On-chain flow growth slowed from 2.6x year-over-year in Q1 to 1.6x in Q2.
Ethereum handles 62% of the volume while Layer 2 chains (networks built atop Ethereum for cheaper transactions) remain immaterial for payment settlement.

items.title: Robinhood Chain leads L2 revenue but barely moves the needle
points: Launched July 1, Robinhood Chain led all tracked Layer 2s with $3.6M revenue in its first month.
Annualized chain revenue is only ~$54.8M ($43.2M protocol, $10.5M USDG yield on a $333.1M market cap, plus a Lighter perps share) — about 14% of Robinhood's $400M annualized crypto revenue.
Robinhood's Q2 2026 crypto revenue fell 38% year-over-year to $100M, an all-time-low 8% of total revenue, with retail crypto volume at its weakest since Q3 2024.
Memecoins are 51% of onchain spot volume versus 5% for real-world assets; Morpho, integrated into the main app, became the chain's 3rd-largest TVL deployment in a month.
Lighter's wallet-only perpetuals integration drew just 0.2% of its volume despite $25M in LIT incentives, showing distribution beats incentives.

items.title: Bitcoin recovery hinges on seller exhaustion, not new demand
points: Bitcoin ETFs saw net $5B of outflows over 52 weeks, with front-end implied volatility at multi-year lows and futures basis unable to clear T-bill yield parity.

On-chain metrics sit in deep-value territory: MVRV (market value to realized value — how far price sits above holders' average purchase price) is at accumulation levels and spot turnover is at all-time lows.
The DAT (digital asset trust) supply overhang is unwinding as treasury companies slow or reverse BTC buying, while long-term holders absorb supply.
BTC remains pinned below its 200-week exponential moving average; large asset manager allocations are the main upside catalyst.
Suggested playbook: dollar-cost-average (invest fixed amounts on a schedule) into spot or buy cheap implied volatility via options.

items.title: Crypto payment card volume hits $759M in July
points: Volume rose 2.5x year-over-year from $306M, across nearly 9M transactions averaging $86 each, up from under $1M when tracking began in October 2023.
Settlement concentrates on Optimism (29%), Solana (19%) and Base (19%).
USDC handles 58% of card spend and USDT 26% (from 48% and 7% a year ago), while euro stablecoin EURe collapsed from 88% in early 2024 to ~2%.
Cards convert stablecoins to local fiat at checkout over Visa rails, giving holders dollar access without a bank account, though volumes remain far below legacy card networks.
USDT supply shrank $4B in 60 days, including $870M in the past 11 days, hinting at tightening stablecoin liquidity.

issues.subject: XRP almost broke $1. Inflation data could finish the job.

headlines: XRP flirted with $1 on Tuesday as leveraged futures bets hit their highest level since October, setting up for outsized moves when CPI inflation data drops today.
A hacker drained $200,000 from an XRP bridge by tricking the software into registering fake deposits as real, then withdrawing actual tokens against non-existent balances.

Fidelity filed to add staking (securing the network by locking up tokens to validate transactions and earn rewards) and quarterly cash distributions to its $898 million ether ETF, transforming it from a passive price tracker into a yield-bearing product.

sections.title: XRP at Critical Price Level Ahead of Inflation Report
points: 1. XRP briefly touched 99 cents on Tuesday—its lowest level since November 2024—before bouncing to $1.02, but the recovery stalled there.
2. Open interest in XRP futures climbed to 2.67 billion XRP ($2.73 billion), the highest since October, meaning massive leveraged bets are stacked at this psychologically critical price.

3. July CPI forecast calls for 0.1% monthly growth and year-on-year inflation dropping to 3.4%; a hotter reading could push XRP below $1 with next support at 92 cents (July 2023 high), while a softer reading could weaken the dollar and trigger a rally.
4. Options market is pricing only a 1.3% post-CPI swing for bitcoin, suggesting traders expect minimal drama—exactly the setup that often produces surprises.

sections.title: XRP Bridge Exploited via Fake Deposit Verification Loophole
points: 1. Attacker drained nearly 200,000 XRP ($200,000) by manipulating the bridge's relayer code to register transactions as deposits without actually delivering XRP to the reserve wallet.

2. The bridge then issued valid receipt tokens for these empty deposits, which the attacker redeemed for real XRP; the 17 of 28 relayers approved each payout because their records showed legitimate deposits.
3. The exploit ran for 97 minutes on August 9, exploiting a failure in the relayer code that processed bridge memos without verifying the destination address.

4. tx (the bridge operator) halted the bridge, patched the vulnerability, and engaged forensics specialists; most stolen XRP moved quickly through multiple addresses with ChangeNOW freezing a portion.

sections.title: Fidelity Ether ETF to Add Staking Rewards and Quarterly Distributions
points: 1. Fidelity filed to allow its Ethereum Fund (FETH, $898 million in assets) to stake up to 100% of its ether holdings, keeping some liquid for redemptions and expenses.

2. The fund would retain 85% of gross staking rewards after payments to node operators (Blockdaemon, Figment, Galaxy), with net rewards covering fund expenses and then flowing to investors as quarterly cash distributions.

3. An IRS safe harbor issued in November 2025 enabled this move by allowing crypto trusts to stake without losing grantor-trust tax status that underpins ETFs; Grayscale and 21Shares already added staking, while BlackRock launched a separate staking product.

4. The shift transforms ether ETFs from passive price trackers into dividend-paying products, giving ether a structural advantage over bitcoin (which cannot be staked) at a moment when ether has underperformed.

issues.subject: The SEC Is About to Propose a Token Safe Harbor

headlines: SEC plans to propose a token safe harbor framework that would create clearer regulatory pathways for cryptocurrency projects and reduce legal uncertainty in the industry.
The safe harbor would establish specific conditions tokens must meet to avoid being classified as securities, addressing years of ambiguity that has stalled project launches and innovation.
New framework aims to balance investor protection with innovation by setting objective criteria for token classification rather than case-by-case regulatory enforcement.
Safe harbor proposal represents significant shift in SEC's approach after previously using enforcement actions to define crypto's regulatory boundaries.

sections.title: Token Safe Harbor Framework Details
points: 1. SEC proposes creating defined conditions that tokens can meet to automatically avoid securities classification, reducing legal risk for token issuers.
2. Framework would establish objective criteria for assessment rather than relying on subjective regulatory interpretation or enforcement precedent.
3. Proposal aims to provide clarity for projects deciding whether to launch tokens domestically or seek international venues with friendlier regulations.
4. Safe harbor would allow tokens meeting criteria to operate without registration while still maintaining investor protection standards.

sections.title: Regulatory and Market Impact
points: 1. Current uncertainty has caused many crypto projects to avoid U.S. markets or delay token launches indefinitely due to fear of SEC enforcement.
2. Clear regulatory pathway could unlock significant innovation and capital formation in the U.S. crypto sector, reversing recent brain drain to other jurisdictions.
3. Proposal signals major policy shift from SEC's enforcement-focused approach toward proactive rule-making that benefits industry participants.
4. Framework may serve as template for international regulators developing their own token classification standards.

issues.subject: ETH Roadmap Update 🗺️, EIP-8363💰, Mastercard and BVNK 📇

headlines: Vitalik Buterin released Ethereum's 2026 Strawmap with seven new technical priorities including quantum-resistant signatures, zero-knowledge proof improvements (SNARKs—cryptographic proofs allowing verification without revealing data), and protocol-level privacy, marking a significant strategic shift from the 2023 roadmap.

EIP-8363 would cut Ethereum staking rewards to zero net issuance at 60.25M ETH staked (~50% of supply), reducing validator income by ~50%, but risks destabilizing $2.6B in stablecoin debt and $40B in TVL dependent on staking yields without modeling the downstream credit market effects.

Mastercard's $1.8B BVNK acquisition closed with $23B in trailing twelve-month settlement volume, but on-chain flow growth plateaued from 2.6x YoY in Q1 to 1.6x in Q2, with Ethereum handling 62% of volume while Layer 2 blockchains remain immaterial to payment settlement.

Robinhood Chain launched July 1 and led all Layer 2 blockchains in first-month revenue at $3.6M, but the chain generates only ~$54.8M annualized revenue (14% of Robinhood's $400M crypto revenue), leaving it immaterial to company fundamentals despite leading memcoin speculation.

Bitcoin ETF outflows of $5B over 52 weeks and on-chain metrics at multi-year lows (MVRV at accumulation levels, spot turnover at all-time lows) suggest recovery depends on seller exhaustion and large asset manager allocation increases rather than new demand.

sections.title: 1. Ethereum's 2026 Technical Roadmap Overhaul
points: Seven new categories added including native rollups enabled by SNARK maturity, blob and gas futures (mechanisms for dynamic pricing of blockchain resources), and zkzk frames exposing non-EVM instruction sets (leanISA and RISC-V candidates) at protocol level, moving EVM from enshrined feature to intermediate representation.
Quantum safety elevated to first-class priority backed by leanSPHINCS signatures and post-quantum aggregation, reflecting heightened focus on protecting against future quantum computing threats.

Privacy receives protocol-level treatment via keyed nonces, recent roots, FOCIL components, lean privacy pools, and wormholes; recursive STARKs (scalable transparent arguments of knowledge—proofs that compress computation verification) now span execution, consensus, and data layers through unified verification primitives.

State expiry replaced with new specialized state types optimized for high-volume use cases (token transfers, swaps, privacy protocols); VDFs (verifiable delay functions) and many EVM improvements deprioritized in favor of scaling and privacy infrastructure.

sections.title: 2. EIP-8363 Staking Reward Taper Risks Onchain Credit Markets
points: EIP-8363 would taper consensus rewards to zero net issuance (no new ETH created from validation) at 60.25M ETH staked (~50% of total supply), cutting validator income roughly 50% at current stake levels while leaving MEV (maximal extractable value—profits validators capture by ordering/including transactions strategically) untouched, increasing MEV's share of validator revenue.

Credit markets priced off staking yields would compress: liquid staking token (LST) looping (borrowing stablecoins against LST collateral to re-stake and amplify yield) drives most ETH lending yield, but neither EIP-8363 nor cited research models how borrowers would repay WETH debt, reduce lending utilization, and push deposit APY down faster than staking yield when spreads compress.

LSTs comprise ~40% of onchain total value locked (TVL), $2.6B in stablecoin debt is collateralized by ETH/LST, and $11.4B in ETF and treasury inflows hold 7.8M ETH—taper puts large portion of Ethereum's TVL lead at risk without modeled justification.

Post-Merge net ETH issuance already runs at 0.30% per year, below Bitcoin (0.82%), gold (1.7%), and M2 expansion (5.5%); authors recommend modeling MEV burn first and staking-yield-dependent lending markets before revisiting issuance.

sections.title: 3. Robinhood Chain's Revenue Impact Overstated
points: Robinhood's Q2 2026 crypto revenue fell 38% year-over-year to $100M and dropped to 8% of total revenue—an all-time low 7% share of assets under custody, with retail crypto volume at lowest level since Q3 2024.

Robinhood Chain launched July 1 and led all tracked Layer 2s with $3.6M in revenue the first month, but known annualized chain revenue totals roughly $54.8M ($43.2M protocol revenue, $10.5M from USDG yield on $333.1M market cap, plus Lighter perps share)—approximately 14% of Robinhood's $400M annualized crypto revenue.

Memecoins drove 51% of onchain spot volume while real-world assets (RWAs) accounted for just 5%; Morpho integrated into main Robinhood app reached the chain's 3rd-largest TVL deployment within one month, demonstrating main-app distribution determines whether chain activity scales.

Lighter's wallet-only perpetuals integration attracted just 0.2% of its volume despite $25M in LIT token incentives, indicating onchain distribution alone cannot drive adoption without main-platform integration.

sections.title: 4. Bitcoin's Recovery Depends on Seller Exhaustion, Not New Demand
points: Bitcoin ETFs logged net $5B in outflows over 52 weeks while front-end implied volatility sits at multi-year lows and BTC futures basis cannot clear T-bill yield parity (basis cannot justify the cost of financing long positions)—quantifying demand deficit that has pinned BTC below its 200-week exponential moving average.

On-chain metrics cluster at deep-value territory: MVRV (market value to realized value ratio measuring how much current price exceeds average acquisition price) is at accumulation-zone levels, spot turnover relative to market cap sits at all-time lows, and on-chain derivative positioning reflects capitulation.

DAT (digital asset trust) supply overhang that pressured price through late 2024 and 2025 is unwinding as treasury companies slow or reverse BTC accumulation; long-term holders are absorbing supply aggressively, indicating whale consolidation rather than retail demand.

Recovery is a seller exhaustion event rather than demand-led rally; large asset manager portfolio allocations are the primary upside catalyst; recommendation is to dollar-cost-average (DCA—invest fixed amounts regularly) spot or buy cheap implied volatility via options over coming months.

sections.title: 5. Crypto Payment Cards Growing on Stablecoin Momentum
points: Crypto payment card volume reached $759M in July, up 2.5x year-over-year from $306M and from sub-$1M at tracking inception in October 2023, across nearly 9M transactions averaging $86 each; settlement concentrates on Optimism (29%), Solana (19%), and Base (19%).

Dollar-backed stablecoins have displaced euro alternatives: USDC handles 58% of card spend and USDT 26% (versus 48% and 7% one year prior), while EURe collapsed from 88% in early 2024 to ~2% today, reflecting global shift toward USD settlement.

Cards convert stablecoins to local fiat at point-of-sale via Visa rails, allowing holders to access dollar accounts without traditional bank accounts; however, monthly card volume remains orders of magnitude below trillions processed by legacy card networks.
USDT supply shrunk $4B over 60 days (including $870M in the past 11 days), suggesting tightening stablecoin liquidity amid broader market consolidation.
